Android phones

Next, we'll update your existing vite.config.js safely and add the PartyVerse app manifest using the official vite-plugin-pwa documentation.

Step 2 — Configure Vite for PartyVerse PWA

Now we'll connect the plugin to your existing Vite configuration. The plugin generates the web app manifest and service worker during production builds.

GitHub
+1

2.1 Open vite.config.js

Your project root should look something like this:

Plain text
PartyVerse/ ├── public/ ├── src/ ├── index.html ├── package.json └── vite.config.js

Open vite.config.js.

2.2 Replace its contents

If your file is named vite.config.js, replace its contents with:

JavaScript

import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { VitePWA } from "vite-plugin-pwa";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    VitePWA({
      registerType: "autoUpdate",

      includeAssets: ["favicon.ico"],

      manifest: {
        name: "PartyVerse - Party Games",
        short_name: "PartyVerse",
        description:
          "Play fun party games with your friends, all in one place.",
        theme_color: "#241d3b",
        background_color: "#f8f7ff",
        display: "standalone",
        orientation: "portrait",
        start_url: "/",
        scope: "/",

        icons: [
          {
            src: "/pwa-192x192.png",
            sizes: "192x192",
            type: "image/png",
          },
          {
            src: "/pwa-512x512.png",
            sizes: "512x512",
            type: "image/png",
          },
          {
            src: "/pwa-512x512.png",
            sizes: "512x512",
            type: "image/png",
            purpose: "any maskable",
          },
        ],
      },
    }),
  ],
});

Important: This configuration assumes your existing project uses @vitejs/plugin-react, which is typical for your React + Vite setup. If your current vite.config.js contains other important configuration, preserve it rather than overwriting it blindly.

2.3 Create the icon files

The configuration references two image paths. We need to create these files next:

Plain text
public/pwa-192x192.png public/pwa-512x512.png

Both should be square PNG icons. The 512×512 icon can also be used as a maskable icon, though a dedicated maskable icon is preferable for polished results.

Don't deploy yet: missing icons can cause manifest warnings or broken app icons.

Your turn

Save vite.config.js and tell me “done”. Next, we'll create the PartyVerse app icon and add both PNG files to public/.
